name: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework (FSF)
description: Google DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework (May 2024) defines critical safety behaviors any frontier AI lab should meet, plus a two-tier concern-level system (Level 1: enhanced monitoring; Level 2: development/deployment halt) triggered by dangerous-capability evaluations. We treat each critical behavior as a criterion: does the company publicly claim a posture that addresses it?

criteria.name: Scheduled dangerous-capability evaluations
criteria.bar: Run pre-deployment and in-deployment evaluations for dangerous capabilities (CBRN, cyber, autonomy) on a defined schedule. Bar: publicly state a commitment to scheduled model evaluations for dangerous capabilities before deployment and at defined capability checkpoints.

criteria.name: CBRN uplift prevention
criteria.bar: Commit to not providing serious uplift toward creation of weapons capable of mass casualties (CBRN: chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear). Bar: a named, public prohibition on CBRN-uplifting use cases backed by a stated detection/filtering mechanism.

criteria.name: Oversight preservation
criteria.bar: Commit to not undermining human ability to oversee, correct, or shut down AI models. Bar: a public statement affirming that the company will not deploy or support systems that actively evade correction or oversight mechanisms, with a stated mechanism for this.

criteria.name: Unsanctioned autonomy / power-seizure prevention
criteria.bar: Commit to preventing AI from engaging in or assisting attempts to seize unprecedented societal control or accumulate resources beyond sanctioned limits. Bar: public policy or framework language explicitly covering autonomous action limits and power-accumulation safeguards.

criteria.name: Threshold-based deployment halt
criteria.bar: Define pre-specified concern levels where development or deployment pauses until safeguards are in place. Bar: a public commitment to halt or restrict deployment when a named threshold (capability evaluation result, concern level, or equivalent) is crossed, before safeguards exist.
